properties.name: The Rainbow Serpent
properties.summary: In the Dreamtime, the Rainbow Serpent slithered across the flat land, creating rivers, valleys, and ridges with its massive body. It established the laws of behavior and consequence. Those who obey prosper; those who break the law are turned to stone. It still sleeps in waterways, maintaining the natural order.

properties.name: The Songlines — Walking the Dreaming
properties.summary: During the Dreaming, Ancestor Beings walked across Australia singing the world into existence. Each feature — rock, waterhole, hill — was created by their songs. Aboriginal people maintain these songlines as navigational paths, spiritual practices, and legal codes. Walking a songline connects past creation with present reality.

properties.name: How Fire Was Stolen (Aboriginal)
properties.summary: In various Aboriginal traditions, fire was guarded by selfish keepers. Crow (or other clever animals) devised schemes to steal it for the people. In one version, Crow tricked the fire-keepers into opening their sacred box, grabbed a burning stick, and flew away, scorching his feathers permanently black.

properties.name: The Seven Sisters (Pleiades)
properties.summary: Across Aboriginal Australia, the Pleiades are seven sisters fleeing a persistent hunter (Orion). They travel across the land, creating landmarks as they go. When he gets too close, they fly into the sky to escape. The hunter follows, forever chasing them across the heavens. The story maps onto real geography and star movements.

properties.name: Crow and the Seven Emu Women
properties.summary: Crow was clever but hungry. He discovered the Emu Women had fire but wouldn't share. He prepared a fake wound full of ants and pretended to be injured. When the women came to help, he tricked them into gathering sticks. He stole their hidden firestick and flew away, but dropped embers across creation, giving fire to all.
